name: Guam
prevalence_note: Guam Homeland Security and the Mariana Regional Fusion Center report scam calls from local, domestic and international numbers, including fake prize wins paid in gift cards; US postal inspectors also warn about fake USPS tracking texts.
cross_border_note: Guam (+1-671) is in the NANP, so spoofed +1 numbers look domestic, while its location in the western Pacific also exposes residents to calls from Asian country codes.

scams.name: Fake prize call asking for gift cards
scams.name_en: Call claiming a big prize win and asking for gift-card codes, flagged by Guam Homeland Security

red_flag_keywords.text: buy gift cards and send the code
meet to sign documents for your winnings

scams.signals_en: A caller says the owner won a large sum, drops the names of the Governor's office or Guam Homeland Security, and asks for gift-card codes or a meeting to sign papers.
scams.legit_en: GHS/OCD and the Mariana Regional Fusion Center say not to give personal or financial data to unexpected callers, and that local numbers can be spoofed.
bait_tactics: Ask which contest was entered and when, then ask for the company's mailing address
Say every prize letter is handed to a family member in Tamuning to look over

scams.name: Fake USPS delivery text
scams.name_en: Fake USPS tracking text reaching Guam residents
scams.signals_en: A text says a USPS package to Guam is held for an incomplete address and links to a page asking for card data.
scams.legit_en: USPIS notes USPS sends tracking texts only when a customer requested them with a tracking number.
bait_tactics: Ask for the tracking number and compare it digit by digit with a printed receipt
Say mainland parcels are always collected at the Guam main facility counter
